_spec: Violation brief for VIOL_mc99v001. Violation briefs are human-readable summaries of each violation, consolidating all traceability paths into a single auditable document. They do NOT add new legal conclusions — they summarize what the graph already contains. Use briefs for review and reporting; use the canonical output for machine processing.
allegation_summary: Carrier failed to rebut its liability for delay under MC99 Art.19 by taking all reasonably required measures to avoid or mitigate damage. Specifically, the carrier did not offer rerouting or any alternative remedy when the passenger's missed connection was caused by an airline-controlled delay.

legal_basis.article_reference: Montreal Convention 1999, Chapter III, Article 19 — Delay
legal_basis.relevant_excerpt: The carrier is liable for damage occasioned by delay... [the carrier] shall not be liable... if it proves that it and its servants and agents took all measures that could reasonably be required to avoid the damage.
legal_basis.nexus: The carrier failed to take reasonable measures (Art.19 rebuttal test): it did not offer rerouting, refused the refund, and directed the passenger to a written complaint process. No mitigation attempt was made.

factual_basis.description: Carrier agent verbally denied passenger's request for rerouting and refused to process a refund.

grounding_segment.text: Carrier denies rerouting and refuses to refund.
grounding_segment.speaker: airline_staff

cross_jurisdiction_note: MC99 (INT) applies to this BR-jurisdiction case via ApplicabilityBasis APPL_intc0001 (basis_type: 'international_air_carriage'). The flight was an international route operated by a Brazilian carrier — MC99 Art.1(1) governs all international carriage of passengers.
